sets.name: 1 · Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties

questions.question:
Match the following:
List-I (Rights)
(a) Right to Constitutional Remedies
(b) Right to Freedom of Religion
(c) Right Against Exploitation
(d) Right to Equality
List-II (Articles)
(i) Articles 25 - 28
(ii) Article 32
(iii) Articles 14 - 18
(iv) Articles 23 - 24

options.A: a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
options.B: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
options.C: a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
options.D: a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Equality 14–18, Freedom 19–22, Exploitation 23–24, Religion 25–28, Cultural & educational 29–30, Remedies 32. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy has been added by 42nd Amendment to the Constitution?

options.C: To secure opportunities for healthy development of children
options.D: To prohibit the slaughter of cows

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Art. 39(f) (healthy development of children), 39A (free legal aid), 43A (workers in management) and 48A (environment). Village panchayats (Art. 40) and Art. 48 were in the original Constitution. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Who has the power to prescribe qualifications to acquire Indian citizenship?
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Art. 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law – the Citizenship Act, 1955. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the sources with the features that have been borrowed in the Indian Constitution:
List I (Source)
a. Constitution of Ireland
b. Constitution of Australia
c. Constitution of France
d. Constitution of South Africa
List II (Borrowed feature)
i. Concurrent List
ii. Procedure for amending the Constitution and the procedure for electing members of the Rajya Sabha
iii. Directive Principles of State Policy
iv. Liberty and Fraternity in the Preamble
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Ireland – DPSP; Australia – Concurrent List; France – Republic, liberty, equality, fraternity; South Africa – amendment procedure, election of Rajya Sabha members. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Read the statements with regard to the Directive Principles of State Policy:
a. The Directive Principles of State Policy are incorporated in Part IV of the Constitution.
b. The Directive Principles of State Policy are legally enforceable.
c. The Directive Principles of State Policy are legally justiciable.
Identify the correct statement/s:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: DPSPs (Arts 36–51, Part IV) are non-justiciable (Art. 37). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not a characteristic of a federal system?

options.C: There is no decentralization of power

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Federalism divides power between the Centre and states; India is 'a Union of States' with a unitary bias. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by the:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). The Preamble has been amended only once. The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) held that it is part of the Constitution (Berubari, 1960, had said it was not).

questions.question: Free and compulsory education for children of 6–14 years became a Fundamental Right under:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: The RTE Act came into force on 1 April 2010; Art. 45 now covers early childhood care for children below six.

questions.question:
Match the writs with their meaning:
a. Habeas corpus
b. Mandamus
c. Quo warranto
d. Certiorari

1. 'To be certified' – quashing an order of a lower court
2. 'By what authority' – against usurping a public office
3. 'To have the body' – against illegal detention
4. 'We command' – to perform a public duty
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Prohibition stops a lower court from continuing a case. The Supreme Court issues writs under Art. 32, High Courts under Art. 226.

questions.question: 'Untouchability' is abolished and its practice forbidden in any form under:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Art. 18 abolishes titles; Art. 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added on the recommendation of the:

options.D: Swaran Singh Committee, by the 42nd Amendment

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Ten duties were added in 1976; the 11th (parents to provide education to children 6–14) came with the 86th Amendment, 2002. Borrowed from the USSR.

questions.question: The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now a constitutional right under:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Art. 265 – no tax except by authority of law.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights are available ONLY to citizens of India?
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Arts 14, 20, 21, 22 and 25–28 are available to foreigners too (except enemy aliens).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Directive Principles cannot be enforced by any court.
Reason (R): Article 37 says they are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: R is the exact reason given in the Constitution.

questions.question: The Uniform Civil Code for citizens is mentioned in:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Goa already has a common civil code; Uttarakhand passed a UCC law in 2024.

questions.question: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called which Article 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'?
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Art. 32 – right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: India's system of single citizenship was borrowed from the constitution of:
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). UK also gave parliamentary government, rule of law and the writs.

questions.question: Article 19 originally guaranteed seven freedoms. How many does it guarantee now?
questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: The freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property (19(1)(f)) was deleted in 1978.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way of losing Indian citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955?

options.A: Failing to vote in two general elections

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Citizenship is acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Right to Education is a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
Reason (R): The 42nd Amendment moved 'education' from the State List to the Concurrent List.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Preamble, Citizenship, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Duties
questions.explanation: Both are true, but the shift to the Concurrent List (1976) is not why education became a Fundamental Right (86th Amendment, 2002).

notes.title: Indian Constitution – revision notes (FRs, legislature, executive, judiciary)
notes.md:
## 1. Sources
| Source | Borrowed |
|---|---|
| UK | parliamentary system, single citizenship, rule of law, writs |
| USA | Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment, independent judiciary |
| Ireland | DPSP, nomination to RS, President's election method |
| Australia | Concurrent List, joint sitting, trade & commerce |
| Canada | federation with strong Centre, residuary powers with Centre |
| France | Republic, liberty-equality-fraternity |
| South Africa | amendment procedure, election of RS members |
| USSR | Fundamental Duties, justice in Preamble |

## 2. Fundamental Rights (Part III)
| Right | Articles |
|---|---|
| Equality | 14–18 (17 untouchability, 18 titles) |
| Freedom | 19–22 (21 life & liberty; 21A education – 86th Amdt 2002) |
| Against exploitation | 23–24 |
| Religion | 25–28 |
| Cultural & educational | 29–30 |
| Constitutional remedies | 32 ('heart and soul' – Ambedkar) |
- Only to citizens: **15, 16, 19, 29, 30**
- Property: removed by 44th Amdt 1978 → **Art. 300A**
- Writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto (SC – 32, HC – 226, wider)

## 3. DPSP (Part IV, 36–51) and Duties (51A)
- Non-justiciable (Art. 37); 40 – village panchayats; 44 – UCC; 45 – early childhood care; 48 – agriculture/cows; 48A – environment
- 42nd Amdt added 39(f), 39A, 43A, 48A
- Duties: Swaran Singh Committee, 42nd Amdt 1976 (10) + 86th 2002 (11th)
- Preamble amended once (42nd: socialist, secular, integrity); part of Constitution – Kesavananda 1973

## 4. Union and state executive / legislature
| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| President's election | elected MPs + elected MLAs (incl. Delhi, Puducherry) |
| Impeachment (61) | violation of the Constitution |
| VP | ex-officio RS Chairman; elected by all MPs |
| Money Bill (110) | Speaker certifies; RS delay 14 days |
| Joint sitting (108) | Speaker presides; not for Money/Amendment Bills; held 1961, 1978, 2002 |
| RS nominated | 12 (Art. 80) |
| Ordinance | 123 (President), 213 (Governor) |
| Council of Ministers | ≤ 15% of house (91st Amdt 2003) |
| Reserved LS seats | SC 84, ST 47 |
| Legislative Council (171) | 1/3 local bodies, 1/3 MLAs, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/6 nominated by **Governor** |
| Karnataka | Assembly 224, Council 75 |
| Law-making | 1st reading → 2nd → committee → report → 3rd |
- Speakers: Shivraj Patil 10th LS, Balayogi 12th, Meira Kumar 15th, Om Birla 17th & 18th
- Calling attention – Indian innovation since **1954**; Zero Hour – 1962
- Anglo-Indian nomination ended – 104th Amdt 2020

## 5. Judiciary and bodies
| Body | Article / fact |
|---|---|
| Supreme Court | 124; 8 judges (1950) → 34 now; advisory 143; collegium – 2nd Judges case 1993 |
| High Court | 214; Karnataka benches Dharwad & Kalaburagi; Madras bench Madurai |
| Emergency | 352 national, 356 President's Rule, 359 suspend FR enforcement, 360 financial |
| Tribunals | Part XIV-A, 323A/B (42nd Amdt); Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 |
| CAG | 148 |
| EC | 324 (multi-member since 1993) |
| UPSC / SPSC | 315; SPSC appointed by Governor, removed by President |
| Finance Commission | 280; 16th – Arvind Panagariya (2026–31) |
| GST Council | 279A (101st Amdt, 2016) |
| NCST | 338A (89th Amdt 2003, from 2004) |
| NHRC | statutory 1993; chair = retired CJI/SC judge |
| AG / Advocate General | 76 / 165 |
| RTI | 2005; 30 days, life & liberty 48 hours; CIC must not be MP/MLA |
| Karnataka Lokayukta | 1984 Act; Lokpal Act 2013 (first Lokpal P.C. Ghose 2019) |

## ⚠ Traps
- 365 ≠ President's Rule (that is 356); 359 suspends FRs, 360 is financial emergency
- Legislative Council nominees – Governor, not President
- High Court judges CAN be removed (same as SC judges)
- NITI Aayog is not a constitutional body

sets.name: 1 · Union and State Legislature and Executive

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT regarding the Governor?
(a) Governor is an integral part of the state Legislature.
(b) He/She nominates 1/6 of the members of state Legislative Council.
(c) He/She nominates one member from Anglo-Indian community to the state Legislative Assembly.
(d) He/She promulgates Ordinances when the state Legislature is not in session.
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: Anglo-Indian nomination to Lok Sabha and Assemblies ended with the 104th Amendment (2020); ordinances – Art. 213. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: As per Article 330, how many seats can be reserved for SC and ST in the Lok Sabha?
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: After the 2008 delimitation, 84 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for SCs and 47 for STs. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following List I with List II and choose the correct answer.
List I (Speaker): (a) Shivaraj Patil (b) G.M.C. Balayogi (c) Meira Kumar (d) Om Birla
List II (Lok Sabha): (i) Seventeenth Lok Sabha (ii) Fifteenth Lok Sabha (iii) Tenth Lok Sabha (iv) Twelfth Lok Sabha

options.A: a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
options.B: a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
options.C: a - iii, b - iv, c - ii, d - i
options.D: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: Shivraj Patil – 10th; Balayogi – 12th; Meira Kumar (first woman Speaker) – 15th; Om Birla – 17th and 18th. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
(a) The President of India appoints the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha as the Prime Minister.
(b) The Prime Minister is the Head of the country.
(c) The Prime Minister is the Leader of the Lower House of the Parliament.
(d) The Prime Minister is the Chief spokesperson of the Central Government.
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: The President is the head of the State; the PM is the head of the government. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
The correct statements about 'calling attention notice' are
(a) It is a device of calling the attention of a Minister to a matter of urgent public importance.
(b) Its main purpose is to seek an authoritative statement from the Minister.
(c) It does not involve any censure against Government.
(d) It is an Indian innovation in the parliamentary procedure since 1952.
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: It is an Indian innovation, but in use since 1954, not 1952. Zero Hour is also an Indian innovation (1962). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of stage of Law Making in the Indian Parliament?

options.A: Report stage, Committee stage, First reading, Second reading, Third reading
options.B: First reading, Second reading, Third reading, Committee stage, Report stage
options.C: Committee stage, First reading, Second reading, Third reading, Report stage
options.D: First reading, Second reading, Committee stage, Report stage, Third reading

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: Introduction (first reading) → general discussion (second reading) → committee and report (consideration) stages → third reading (passing). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT regarding legislative council?
(a) 1/3 are elected by the members of local bodies.
(b) 1/12 are elected by graduates.
(c) 1/3 are elected by the members of the legislative assembly of the state.
(d) 1/6 are nominated by President.
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: 1/3 local bodies, 1/3 MLAs, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/6 nominated by the GOVERNOR (Art. 171). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which among the following countries have parliamentary system of government?
(a) Britain
(b) India
(c) Brazil
(d) Sri Lanka
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: Brazil has a presidential system and Sri Lanka an executive presidency. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

options.A: Elected members of Lok Sabha and Legislative Councils
options.B: All members of Parliament and all members of state legislatures including nominated members
options.C: All members of both Houses of Parliament only
options.D: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of state Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi and Puducherry)

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not vote; the Vice-President is elected by ALL members of both Houses.

questions.question: The President can be removed by impeachment (Article 61) only for:
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: 'Proved misbehaviour or incapacity' is the ground for removing Supreme Court and High Court judges.

questions.question: The ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is:

options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). The Deputy Chairman is elected from among Rajya Sabha members.

questions.question: Who certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill (Article 110)?

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha can only delay a Money Bill by 14 days; it can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha with the President's recommendation.

questions.question: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Article 108) is presided over by the Speaker and CANNOT be held for:

options.B: A Bill rejected by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: A Money Bill or a Constitution Amendment Bill
options.D: A Bill pending for over six months

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Joint sittings have been held only three times: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission (1978) and POTA (2002).

questions.question: How many members are nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President for their knowledge in literature, science, art and social service?
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: Art. 80; the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is 250.

questions.question: The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha and of the Rajya Sabha respectively is:
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: The President and Vice-President must be at least 35.

questions.question: Ordinances can be issued by the President under Article ____ and by the Governor under Article ____.
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). An ordinance lapses six weeks after the legislature reassembles.

questions.question: The size of the Council of Ministers (including the PM) cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. This was introduced by the:
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: For states, 15% of the Assembly but not fewer than 12 ministers.

questions.question: The Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council have respectively:
questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Karnataka is one of six states with a bicameral legislature; the Council is a permanent house.

questions.question: The Governor of a state is appointed by the President and holds office:

options.A: Until removed by the state Assembly
options.C: During the pleasure of the President (Art. 156)
options.D: For a fixed five-year term that cannot be cut short

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: Arts 153–155; the normal term is five years.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President before its term ends.
Reason (R): The Speaker vacates office immediately on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Union and State Legislature and Executive
questions.explanation: R is false: the Speaker continues until just before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha.

sets.name: 1 · Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration

questions.question:
Read the statements with regard to High Court mentioned below:
(a) The Chief Justice of a High Court can appoint officers and staff of the High Court without any interference from the executive.
(b) The Judges of a High Court are appointed by the President.
(c) The President can transfer a Judge from one High Court to another after consulting the Chief Justice of India.
(d) A Judge of a High Court cannot be removed from his office.
Identify the correct statements
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: A High Court judge can be removed like a Supreme Court judge – by an address of Parliament on proved misbehaviour or incapacity (Arts 217, 218). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following options regarding NHRC is correct?

options.A: Chairman should be a retired Chief Justice of Supreme Court of India or retired Chief Justice of a High Court
options.B: Chairman is appointed by the President on the recommendation of Prime Minister and his Council of Ministers
options.C: It can amend Constitution to safeguard human rights
options.D: It promotes research on human rights

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Since 2019 the chairperson is a retired CJI or Supreme Court judge, appointed on a committee's recommendation (PM, Speaker, Home Minister, opposition leaders, Deputy Chairman of RS); NHRC is statutory (1993). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the constitutional bodies?
(a) NITI Aayog
(b) Finance Commission
(c) GST Council
(d) National Medical Commission
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Finance Commission – Art. 280; GST Council – Art. 279A (101st Amendment). NITI Aayog is an executive body; NMC is statutory (2019). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Independence of State Public Service Commission
(a) Chairpersons and members can only be removed by the President on specific grounds after a Supreme Court inquiry.
(b) Their salaries, allowances and pensions are determined by the Governor but cannot be changed to their disadvantage during their term.
(c) They are ineligible for other Government jobs, limiting potential pressure or inducement.
(d) While appointed by the Governor, the removal process is insulated, emphasizing their independent role.
How many of the above statements is/are correct?

options.A: All the four statements are correct

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Arts 316–319: appointed by the Governor, removed only by the President (misbehaviour after a Supreme Court inquiry); expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Emergency Provisions exercised by the President of India is/are correct?
(a) Under Article 352, the President can declare a National Emergency.
(b) Under Article 365, the President can impose Presidential Rule on any state.
(c) Under Article 356, the President can suspend the fundamental rights of citizens.
(d) Article 359 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency.
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: 352 – National Emergency; 356 – President's Rule; 359 – suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights; 360 – Financial Emergency. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Tribunals in Indian Constitution.
(a) Original constitution provides for the establishment of Tribunals.
(b) Tribunals are mentioned in Part-XIV-A.
(c) Articles 323A and 323B deal with Tribunals.
(d) The Parliament passed the Administrative Tribunals Act in 1985.
Identify the correct statements.
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Part XIV-A (Arts 323A, 323B) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 (Swaran Singh Committee). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (STs):
a. The Commission is a constitutional body.
b. Article 338A provides for the establishment of the Commission.
c. The separate National Commission for STs came into existence in 2004.
d. The President of India is the Chairperson of the Commission.
Identify the correct statements:
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Created by the 89th Amendment (2003), functioning from 2004; its chairperson is appointed by the President. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the pairs and identify the 'incorrect' pair.
List-I (High Court) – List-II (Seat/Bench)
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: The Madras High Court's bench is at Madurai. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Chief Information Commissioner should be a member of Parliament or member of legislature of any state.
Statement-II: He should be a person of eminence in public life with wide knowledge and experience in Law, Science, Technology, Social Service, Management and Administration.

options.A: Statement-I is correct and statement-II is incorrect.
options.B: Statement-II is correct and statement-I is incorrect.
options.C: Both statement-I and statement-II are correct.
options.D: Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect.

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Under the RTI Act, 2005 the CIC must NOT be an MP or MLA or hold any office of profit. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Who appoints the Municipal Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation?
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: The commissioner (usually an IAS officer) is the chief executive appointed by the state government; the Mayor is the elected head. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: At its inauguration in 1950 the Supreme Court had 8 judges (including the CJI). Its present sanctioned strength is:
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Raised from 31 to 34 by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.

questions.question: Which statement about writ jurisdiction is correct?

options.A: High Courts (Art. 226) can issue writs for Fundamental Rights and also for other legal rights
options.B: Only the Supreme Court can issue writs
options.C: The Supreme Court can issue writs for any legal right under Art. 32
options.D: Writs are issued only by tribunals

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Art. 32 is limited to Fundamental Rights, so the High Courts' writ jurisdiction is wider.

questions.question: The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, under which the President may seek its opinion, is in:
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). 131 – original jurisdiction (Centre–state disputes); 137 – review; 129 – court of record.

questions.question: The 'collegium' system of appointing judges evolved from the:
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: The Third Judges case (1998) expanded it to the CJI and four senior-most judges; the NJAC (99th Amendment) was struck down in 2015.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (Art. 148) submits his audit reports on the Union's accounts to:

options.C: The President, who lays them before Parliament

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). The Public Accounts Committee examines them; the CAG is called the 'guardian of the public purse'.

questions.question: Which statement about the Election Commission of India is correct?

options.A: It conducts panchayat elections in every state
options.B: It became a multi-member body in 1993 and works under Article 324
options.C: The CEC can be removed by the President at will
options.D: Its members are elected by Parliament

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: Panchayat and municipal elections are run by State Election Commissions (Art. 243K); the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge.

questions.question: The 16th Finance Commission, which made recommendations for 2026–31, was chaired by:
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). N.K. Singh chaired the 15th; Finance Commissions are set up every five years under Art. 280.

questions.question: Which of these is a statutory anti-corruption body in Karnataka?
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in 2013; India's first Lokpal was Justice P.C. Ghose (2019).

questions.question: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be supplied within:
questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Ordinary requests: 30 days; first appeal to the departmental appellate authority, second to the Information Commission.

questions.question: The Attorney General of India (Art. 76) and the Advocate General of a state (Art. 165) are appointed respectively by:

options.C: The Prime Minister and the Chief Minister
options.D: The Chief Justice and the High Court

questions.subject: Judiciary, Constitutional Bodies and Public Administration
questions.explanation: The Attorney General can speak in either House of Parliament but cannot vote.

notes.title: Indian Constitution – revision notes (FRs, legislature, executive, judiciary)
notes.md:
## 1. Sources
| Source | Borrowed |
|---|---|
| UK | parliamentary system, single citizenship, rule of law, writs |
| USA | Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment, independent judiciary |
| Ireland | DPSP, nomination to RS, President's election method |
| Australia | Concurrent List, joint sitting, trade & commerce |
| Canada | federation with strong Centre, residuary powers with Centre |
| France | Republic, liberty-equality-fraternity |
| South Africa | amendment procedure, election of RS members |
| USSR | Fundamental Duties, justice in Preamble |

## 2. Fundamental Rights (Part III)
| Right | Articles |
|---|---|
| Equality | 14–18 (17 untouchability, 18 titles) |
| Freedom | 19–22 (21 life & liberty; 21A education – 86th Amdt 2002) |
| Against exploitation | 23–24 |
| Religion | 25–28 |
| Cultural & educational | 29–30 |
| Constitutional remedies | 32 ('heart and soul' – Ambedkar) |
- Only to citizens: **15, 16, 19, 29, 30**
- Property: removed by 44th Amdt 1978 → **Art. 300A**
- Writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto (SC – 32, HC – 226, wider)

## 3. DPSP (Part IV, 36–51) and Duties (51A)
- Non-justiciable (Art. 37); 40 – village panchayats; 44 – UCC; 45 – early childhood care; 48 – agriculture/cows; 48A – environment
- 42nd Amdt added 39(f), 39A, 43A, 48A
- Duties: Swaran Singh Committee, 42nd Amdt 1976 (10) + 86th 2002 (11th)
- Preamble amended once (42nd: socialist, secular, integrity); part of Constitution – Kesavananda 1973

## 4. Union and state executive / legislature
| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| President's election | elected MPs + elected MLAs (incl. Delhi, Puducherry) |
| Impeachment (61) | violation of the Constitution |
| VP | ex-officio RS Chairman; elected by all MPs |
| Money Bill (110) | Speaker certifies; RS delay 14 days |
| Joint sitting (108) | Speaker presides; not for Money/Amendment Bills; held 1961, 1978, 2002 |
| RS nominated | 12 (Art. 80) |
| Ordinance | 123 (President), 213 (Governor) |
| Council of Ministers | ≤ 15% of house (91st Amdt 2003) |
| Reserved LS seats | SC 84, ST 47 |
| Legislative Council (171) | 1/3 local bodies, 1/3 MLAs, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/6 nominated by **Governor** |
| Karnataka | Assembly 224, Council 75 |
| Law-making | 1st reading → 2nd → committee → report → 3rd |
- Speakers: Shivraj Patil 10th LS, Balayogi 12th, Meira Kumar 15th, Om Birla 17th & 18th
- Calling attention – Indian innovation since **1954**; Zero Hour – 1962
- Anglo-Indian nomination ended – 104th Amdt 2020

## 5. Judiciary and bodies
| Body | Article / fact |
|---|---|
| Supreme Court | 124; 8 judges (1950) → 34 now; advisory 143; collegium – 2nd Judges case 1993 |
| High Court | 214; Karnataka benches Dharwad & Kalaburagi; Madras bench Madurai |
| Emergency | 352 national, 356 President's Rule, 359 suspend FR enforcement, 360 financial |
| Tribunals | Part XIV-A, 323A/B (42nd Amdt); Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 |
| CAG | 148 |
| EC | 324 (multi-member since 1993) |
| UPSC / SPSC | 315; SPSC appointed by Governor, removed by President |
| Finance Commission | 280; 16th – Arvind Panagariya (2026–31) |
| GST Council | 279A (101st Amdt, 2016) |
| NCST | 338A (89th Amdt 2003, from 2004) |
| NHRC | statutory 1993; chair = retired CJI/SC judge |
| AG / Advocate General | 76 / 165 |
| RTI | 2005; 30 days, life & liberty 48 hours; CIC must not be MP/MLA |
| Karnataka Lokayukta | 1984 Act; Lokpal Act 2013 (first Lokpal P.C. Ghose 2019) |

## ⚠ Traps
- 365 ≠ President's Rule (that is 356); 359 suspends FRs, 360 is financial emergency
- Legislative Council nominees – Governor, not President
- High Court judges CAN be removed (same as SC judges)
- NITI Aayog is not a constitutional body

questions.question: According to Article 368 of Indian Constitution, changes in which of the following is not considered as an Amendment to Indian Constitution?

options.A: Election process of President of India
options.B: Provisions related to Supreme Court and High Court
options.C: Any of the lists in the Seventh Schedule
options.D: Any entry in the Second Schedule

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: Changes to the Second Schedule (salaries, allowances) are made by a simple law and are 'not deemed an amendment for the purposes of Art. 368'. The President's election, the judiciary and the Seventh Schedule lists need a special majority plus ratification by half the states. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Identify the Article and Part, with reference to Amendment of the Constitution:
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: Part XX has only one Article – 368. Part XXI deals with temporary, transitional and special provisions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding 101st Constitutional Amendment of the Constitution of India:
a. It was passed by the Parliament in 2015.
b. It paved the way for GST.
c. It provided for the establishment of the GST Council.
Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment was passed in 2016 (assent 8 Sep 2016); GST began on 1 July 2017; GST Council – Art. 279A. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992 amends Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?
(a) Konkani
(b) Manipuri
(c) Nepali
(d) Tulu
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: Tulu is not yet in the Eighth Schedule. 21st Amdt (1967) added Sindhi; 92nd (2003) Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali – total 22. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The 97th Constitutional Amendment deals with
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: 97th Amendment (2011): right to form co-operatives in Art. 19(1)(c), Art. 43B and Part IXB. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT with respect to Special Intensive Revision (SIR)?
(a) Every year Election Commission of India conducts this exercise.
(b) The names of new voters who are aged 18+ are being included in the voters list.
(c) It also intends to remove the names of illegal foreign immigrants.
(d) Election Commission of India can conduct SIR exercise if the concerned states give consent.
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: SIR is a special, not annual, revision (summary revision is yearly); the EC conducts it under Art. 324 and the RP Act, 1950 without needing state consent. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment (2019) provided:

options.B: Up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS) in education and public jobs

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Upheld by the Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan (2022). It added Arts 15(6) and 16(6).

questions.question: Which amendment extended SC/ST reservation in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies by ten years and ended nomination of Anglo-Indians?
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: Reservation now runs until January 2030.

questions.question: The 105th Amendment (2021) is about:

options.A: Creating the National Judicial Appointments Commission
options.D: Restoring states' power to prepare their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). It reversed the effect of the Maratha reservation judgment (2021).

questions.question: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 – 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' – provides:

options.B: One-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, after the next census and delimitation
options.C: Reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Women's reservation in central government jobs

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: The reservation will last 15 years and includes seats for SC/ST women; it does not cover the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils.

questions.question: Article 370 relating to Jammu and Kashmir was made inoperative in August 2019. The Supreme Court upheld the decision in:
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). J&K and Ladakh became Union territories on 31 October 2019.

questions.question: The 44th Amendment (1978) made which change to emergency provisions?

options.A: Replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for national emergency
options.C: Allowed suspension of Article 21 during emergency

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: It also said Arts 20 and 21 cannot be suspended and required the Cabinet's written advice for an emergency.

questions.question: The Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) was added by the:
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). The 91st Amendment (2003) removed the 'split' exception; mergers need two-thirds of the legislature party.

questions.question: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the:
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: It came into force in 1989; Art. 326 – adult suffrage.

questions.question: The 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) added respectively:

options.C: Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (panchayats); Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (municipalities)

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: The 11th Schedule lists 29 subjects; the 12th lists 18.

questions.question: The 99th Amendment (2014) creating the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) was:

options.B: Struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015 (Fourth Judges case)

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). The collegium system therefore continues.

questions.question: The National Commission for Backward Classes got constitutional status (Article 338B) through the:
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: 89th Amdt – separate NCST (338A); 65th – National Commission for SCs and STs; 93rd – reservation in private educational institutions (15(5)).

questions.question: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed every year on:
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). The Constitution was adopted on 26 Nov 1949; observed as Constitution Day since 2015. 25 June is 'Samvidhan Hatya Diwas' (from 2024).

questions.question:
Consider the statements about 'One Nation, One Election':
I. A high-level committee on simultaneous elections was chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind.
II. The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill on simultaneous elections was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The Bill proposes Art. 82A for simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the 'Mini-Constitution'.
Reason (R): It made the largest number of changes to the Constitution, including the Preamble, DPSP and Fundamental Duties.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Constitutional Amendments and Recent Developments
questions.explanation: It was based on the Swaran Singh Committee; many changes were reversed by the 43rd and 44th Amendments.

(b) Interstate Council

questions.question: How many Schedules does the Constitution of India have now?
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules

questions.question: How many languages are now in the Eighth Schedule?
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules

questions.question: 'Education' was shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List by the:
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and administration of justice were also moved in 1976.

questions.question:
Match the Parts with their subjects:
a. Part III
b. Part IV
c. Part IVA
d. Part IX

1. Panchayats
2. Fundamental Rights
3. Directive Principles
4. Fundamental Duties
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules
questions.explanation: Part IXA – municipalities; IXB – co-operative societies.

questions.question: Which emergency provision of the Constitution has never been used so far?
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). National emergency was declared in 1962, 1971 and 1975.

questions.question: The right to privacy was declared a Fundamental Right (part of Article 21) in:
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules
questions.explanation: Maneka Gandhi widened 'procedure established by law' to mean fair, just and reasonable procedure.

questions.question: 'Equality before the law' and 'equal protection of the laws' in Article 14 are borrowed respectively from:
questions.subject: Important Articles, Parts and Schedules
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC GK). Equality before law is a negative concept; equal protection a positive one.

questions.question: Article 1 of the Constitution says:

options.A: Hindi shall be the national language
options.B: India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States
options.C: India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic

notes.md:
## 1. Key amendments
| No. | Year | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | 1951 | 9th Schedule (land reforms) |
| 7th | 1956 | states reorganised |
| 42nd | 1976 | 'Mini-Constitution' – socialist, secular, integrity; Fundamental Duties; tribunals; education to Concurrent List |
| 44th | 1978 | property → 300A; 'armed rebellion'; Arts 20, 21 never suspended |
| 52nd | 1985 | Anti-defection (10th Schedule) |
| 61st | 1988 | voting age 21 → 18 |
| 71st | 1992 | Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali in 8th Schedule |
| 73rd / 74th | 1992 | Panchayats (Part IX, 11th Sch) / Municipalities (IXA, 12th Sch) |
| 86th | 2002 | Art. 21A RTE; 11th Fundamental Duty |
| 89th | 2003 | separate NCST (338A) |
| 91st | 2003 | ministers ≤ 15%; split exception removed |
| 92nd | 2003 | Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (22 languages) |
| 97th | 2011 | Co-operative societies (19(1)(c), 43B, Part IXB) |
| 98th | 2012 | Art. 371J – Hyderabad-Karnataka |
| 99th | 2014 | NJAC – struck down 2015 |
| 101st | **2016** | GST; GST Council 279A (GST from 1 Jul 2017) |
| 102nd | 2018 | NCBC – 338B |
| 103rd | 2019 | 10% EWS |
| 104th | 2020 | SC/ST reservation +10 yrs; Anglo-Indian nomination ended |
| 105th | 2021 | states' SEBC lists restored |
| 106th | 2023 | Nari Shakti Vandan – 1/3 women in LS & Assemblies (after census + delimitation, 15 yrs) |

## 2. In the news
- Art. 370 inoperative Aug 2019; SC upheld Dec 2023; J&K, Ladakh UTs from 31 Oct 2019
- One Nation One Election – Kovind committee; 129th Amendment Bill (Dec 2024) → JPC
- Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by ECI – not annual, no state consent needed
- Census 2027 – first digital census, with caste enumeration; census = Union List entry 69
- Constitution Day 26 Nov (since 2015); Samvidhan Hatya Diwas 25 June (from 2024)

## 3. Important Articles
| Art. | Subject | Art. | Subject |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Union of States | 3 | new states |
| 14 | equality | 21 | life, liberty (privacy – Puttaswamy 2017) |
| 32 | constitutional remedies | 40 | village panchayats |
| 44 | UCC | 51A | duties (h – scientific temper) |
| 72 / 161 | pardon | 76 / 165 | AG / Advocate General |
| 110 | Money Bill | 123 / 213 | ordinances |
| 148 | CAG | 239AA | Delhi |
| 243D / I / K | reservation / SFC / SEC | 248 | residuary powers |
| 263 | Inter-State Council | 266 | Consolidated Fund |
| 280 | Finance Commission | 279A | GST Council |
| 312 | All India Services | 315 | PSCs |
| 324 | Election Commission | 343 | Hindi official language |
| 352/356/360 | emergencies | 368 | amendment (Part XX) |
| 371J | Kalyana Karnataka | | |

## 4. Parts and schedules
- 12 Schedules; Part III FR, IV DPSP, IVA duties, IX panchayats, IXA municipalities, IXB co-operatives, XIVA tribunals, XX amendment
- Second Schedule (salaries) changes are not 'amendments' under Art. 368

## ⚠ Traps
- 101st Amendment passed in 2016, not 2015
- Tulu is NOT in the 8th Schedule (demand pending)
- Financial emergency (360) has never been used
